questions.question: Which of the following household items does NOT use the heating effect of current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric motor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy, not heat.
 
• Electric stoves, water heaters, and iron boxes use the heating effect of current to function.
 
• In electric stoves, the current passes through resistive heating elements, generating heat.
 
• Electric water heaters use heating elements that convert electrical energy into heat to warm water.
 
• Electric iron boxes have resistive elements that produce heat to iron clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heating Elements**

 
 
• They are made of materials with high resistivity, such as nichrome, which converts electrical energy into heat efficiently.
 
• Commonly used in household appliances like toasters, hair dryers, and space heaters.
 
 
 
• **Resistive Heating**
 
 
• This is the process by which an electric current passes through a resistive material, causing it to heat up.
 
• It is widely used in various applications, including industrial heating and household appliances.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motors**
 
 
• They are used in a wide range of applications, from household appliances to industrial machinery.
 
• Electric motors work based on electromagnetic induction and do not primarily rely on the heating effect of current.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct according to the law of conservation of mass?

options.text: Mass can be created but cannot be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be created in a chemical reaction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• This principle was established by Antoine Lavoisier in the 18th century.
 
• In a closed system, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
 
• The law applies to both physical changes and chemical reactions.
 
• This law is fundamental to the field of chemistry and underpins stoichiometric calculations in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• It is also known as Proust's law.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**
 
 
• This law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
• It was formulated by John Dalton.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry**
 
 
• It involves the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is based on the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes become half in a daughter cell by the process of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell.
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction and occurs in the germ cells to produce gametes (sperm and eggs).
 
• Meiosis involves two sequential divisions: meiosis I and meiosis II.
 
• During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes are separated, and during meiosis II, sister chromatids are separated.
 
• The reduction in chromosome number ensures that when fertilization occurs, the resulting zygote has the correct diploid number of chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• During binary fission, the parent cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis**
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It is involved in growth, repair, and asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms.
 
 
 
• **Amitosis**
 
 
• Amitosis is a direct method of cell division where the nucleus and cytoplasm divide without the formation of chromosomes.
 
• This process is less common and occurs in some single-celled organisms and certain tissues.

questions.question: Which of the following metals CANNOT be cut with a knife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium, lithium, and potassium are alkali metals that are soft and can be cut with a knife.
 
• Alkali metals are known for their softness and low density.
 
• Copper is a transition metal, which is much harder and cannot be cut with a knife.
 
• The hardness of a metal is determined by its atomic structure and bonding.
 
• Alkali metals have a single electron in their outer shell, which makes them highly reactive and soft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkali Metals**

 
 
• These metals are found in Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• They are highly reactive, especially with water, and are stored in oil to prevent reactions with moisture in the air.
 
• Examples include lithium, sodium, and potassium.
 
 
 
• **Transition Metals**
 
 
• These metals are found in the central block of the periodic table (Groups 3-12).
 
• They are characterized by their ability to form variable oxidation states and colored compounds.
 
• Examples include copper, iron, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Metals and Their Properties**
 
 
• Metals are generally malleable, ductile, and good conductors of electricity and heat.
 
• The physical properties of metals vary widely across the periodic table.
 
• Reactivity, hardness, and melting points of metals can differ significantly based on their atomic structure and bonding.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two objects of masses m₁ and m₂ is directly proportional to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**m₁ × m₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is governed by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.
 
• The formula for gravitational force is F = G * (m₁ * m₂) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two objects (m₁ and m₂).
 
• This means that if either mass increases, the gravitational force between them also increases.
 
• The gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**

 
 
• G is a universal constant with a value of approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N(m/kg)².
 
 
 
• It is a key component in the formula for calculating gravitational force.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**
 
 
• This law states that the force between two masses is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• This means that if the distance is doubled, the gravitational force becomes one-fourth.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Weight**
 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is usually measured in kilograms.
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object and is dependent on both the mass of the object and the gravitational field strength.
 
• Weight can be calculated using the formula Weight = Mass × Gravitational field strength.

questions.question: The magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire at a given point depends on which of the following factors?

options.text: Neither distance from the wire nor current through the wire
Current flowing through the wire Only
Both distance from the wire and current through the wire

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both distance from the wire and current through the wire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire is directly proportional to the current flowing through the wire.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field decreases as the distance from the wire increases.
 
• The relationship between the magnetic field (B), current (I), and distance (r) is given by the Biot-Savart law and Ampère's circuital law.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field can be determined using the right-hand rule: if you point your thumb in the direction of the current, your fingers will curl in the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The magnetic field forms concentric circles around the wire, with the wire itself being at the center of these circles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**

 
 
• It is the process of generating an electromotive force (EMF) or voltage in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field.
 
• This principle is the basis for the operation of transformers, electric generators, and induction motors.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Rule**
 
 
• This is a mnemonic used to determine the direction of the magnetic field relative to the direction of the current.
 
• It states that if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, your fingers will curl in the direction of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux**
 
 
• Magnetic flux is the measure of the quantity of magnetism, taking into account the strength and the extent of a magnetic field.
 
• It is measured in Webers (Wb).
 
• Magnetic flux through a surface is proportional to the number of magnetic field lines passing through that surface.

questions.question: If a force `F` acts on a body such that the body gets displaced through the distance `x` in the direction of the force, then the work done by the force is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fx**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The formula for work done (W) when a force (F) causes a displacement (x) in the direction of the force is given by **W = Fx**.
 
• Work is a scalar quantity and is measured in joules (J) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The displacement must be in the direction of the force for the formula W = Fx to hold true.
 
• If the force and displacement are in the same direction, the work done is positive.
 
• If the force and displacement are in opposite directions, the work done is negative, indicating that the force opposes the motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy**

 
 
• Energy is the ability to do work. It can exist in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, and chemical energy.
 
• Work and energy are closely related; work done on an object transfers energy to the object.
 
 
 
• **Power**
 
 
• Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. It is measured in watts (W) in the SI system.
 
• One watt is equal to one joule per second (J/s).
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy**
 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion. It is given by the formula KE = 0.5 * m * v², where m is mass and v is velocity.
 
• Any object that is moving has kinetic energy.

questions.question: Which of the following options does NOT represent a property of solids?

options.text: It is not difficult to change their shape.
They have distinct boundaries and fixed volumes.
They have a tendency to maintain their shape when subjected to outside force.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is not difficult to change their shape.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Solids have a definite shape that is maintained without external support.
 
• Solids possess fixed volumes and distinct boundaries.
 
• Solids are rigid and resist changes in shape when subjected to external forces.
 
• Particles in solids are closely packed in a fixed arrangement, contributing to their rigidity.
 
• Unlike liquids and gases, solids do not flow and maintain their form unless a significant force is applied.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liquids**

 
 
• They have a definite volume but take the shape of their container.
 
• Particles in liquids are less tightly packed compared to solids, allowing them to flow.
 
 
 
• **Gases**
 
 
• Gases neither have a definite shape nor a fixed volume, expanding to fill their container.
 
• Particles in gases are widely spaced and move freely.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma is an ionized state of matter similar to gas but with charged particles.
 
• It is found naturally in stars, including the sun.

questions.question: Which of the following types of reaction represents formation of slaked lime from calcium oxide and water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• The formation of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) from calcium oxide and water is a classic example of a combination reaction.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
 
• This type of reaction is exothermic, meaning it releases heat.
 
• Combination reactions are also known as synthesis reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition reaction**

 
 
• This type of reaction involves a single compound breaking down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• An example of a decomposition reaction is the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation reaction**
 
 
• In a precipitation reaction, two solutions react to form an insoluble solid, known as the precipitate.
 
• An example is the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride to form silver chloride precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction**
 
 
• This type of reaction involves an element displacing another element in a compound, forming a new compound.
 
• An example is the reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, where zinc displaces hydrogen to form zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.

questions.concept: Transport in Plants, Biology in Everyday life
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of osmosis?

options.text: Absorption of water by plant roots
Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of the living cell
Swelling of raisins when soaked in water
Gaining of water by unicellular fresh water organisms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of the living cell**__.

__**Note**__**:**** **According to the official answer key, the given answer is **Option 4 **but in actual the correct answer would be **Option 2** because movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of living cells is not an example of osmosis; it occurs through the process of diffusion and gaining of water by unicellular freshwater organisms happens through osmosis as water enters the organism from the surrounding environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Osmosis is the process of water molecules moving across a semipermeable membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to an area of higher solute concentration.
 
• Absorption of water by plant roots is an example of osmosis, as water moves from the soil (lower solute concentration) into the roots (higher solute concentration).
 
• Swelling of raisins when soaked in water occurs due to osmosis, where water moves into the raisins causing them to swell.
 
• Gaining of water by unicellular freshwater organisms happens through osmosis as water enters the organism from the surrounding environment.
 
• Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of living cells is not an example of osmosis; it occurs through the process of diffusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffusion**

 
 
• Diffusion is the movement of molecules from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• It does not require a semipermeable membrane and can involve various types of molecules including gases and small solutes.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport is the movement of molecules against their concentration gradient, requiring energy in the form of ATP.
 
• This process is essential for maintaining concentration gradients of ions across cell membranes.
 
 
 
• **Facilitated Diffusion**
 
 
• Facilitated diffusion is a type of passive transport that involves the use of carrier proteins to move molecules across a cell membrane.
 
• It is important for the transport of substances that cannot diffuse freely across the membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is unsaturated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C₂H₄**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Unsaturated compounds contain at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms.
 
• C₂H₄, also known as ethene, is an unsaturated hydrocarbon because it contains a carbon-carbon double bond.
 
• Compounds like C₂H₆ (ethane) and C₃H₈ (propane) are saturated hydrocarbons, meaning they only have single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons are more reactive than saturated hydrocarbons due to the presence of double or triple bonds.
 
• Unsaturated compounds can participate in addition reactions, where the double or triple bonds are broken to add new atoms to the molecule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated Hydrocarbons**

 
 
• These are hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• They are also known as alkanes.
 
• Examples include methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), and propane (C₃H₈).
 
 
 
• **Alkenes**
 
 
• Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond.
 
• They are more reactive than alkanes due to the presence of the double bond.
 
• Ethene (C₂H₄) is the simplest alkene.
 
 
 
• **Alkynes**
 
 
• Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon triple bond.
 
• They are even more reactive than alkenes.
 
• Examples include ethyne (C₂H₂), also known as acetylene.

questions.question: A car moving along a straight path slows down and stops. The car is under which type of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A car slowing down and eventually stopping is an example of **non-uniform motion**, where the speed of the car changes over time.
 
• In non-uniform motion, the velocity of the object is not constant, and there is an acceleration or deceleration involved.
 
• This type of motion can be described by the change in speed and direction, indicating a varying rate of displacement.
 
• Non-uniform motion is often analyzed using kinematic equations that take into account initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Examples of non-uniform motion include a car braking to a stop, a ball rolling down a hill, or a plane taking off and landing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion**

 
 
• In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time without changing its speed or direction.
 
• Examples include a car cruising at a constant speed on a straight road or the Earth orbiting the Sun at a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Circular Motion**
 
 
• This type of motion occurs when an object moves along a circular path at a constant or varying speed.
 
• Examples include the rotation of a fan blade or a satellite orbiting a planet.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Motion**
 
 
• Periodic motion is characterized by the repetition of motion at regular time intervals.
 
• Examples include the swinging of a pendulum or the oscillation of a spring.

questions.question: Which of the following is formed when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide, the product formed is calcium carbonate.
 
• The chemical reaction can be represented as: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O.
 
• This reaction is commonly used in the limewater test for the detection of carbon dioxide gas.
 
• Calcium carbonate is a white, insoluble solid that precipitates out of the solution.
 
• Calcium carbonate is commonly found in rocks as minerals calcite and aragonite, and it is the main component of shells of marine organisms, snails, and eggs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium hydroxide**

 
 
• Also known as slaked lime, it is a chemical compound with the formula Ca(OH)₂.
 
• It is a colorless crystal or white powder and is produced by mixing calcium oxide (lime) with water.
 
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide**
 
 
• A colorless, odorless gas found in Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It is a key component in the process of photosynthesis and is also produced during the respiration of living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Limewater**
 
 
• A saturated solution of calcium hydroxide in water.
 
• It is commonly used as a test for the presence of carbon dioxide, as it turns milky in the presence of CO₂ due to the formation of calcium carbonate.

questions.question: The nature of an image formed by a concave mirror when an object is kept at the position between the principal focus and the pole of the mirror is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the principal focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual and erect.
 
• The image appears on the same side of the mirror as the object.
 
• This virtual image is enlarged compared to the actual object.
 
• Concave mirrors are also known as converging mirrors as they converge light rays that are incident parallel to the principal axis.
 
• Such mirrors are commonly used in applications like shaving mirrors, makeup mirrors, and certain optical instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirrors**

 
 
• Convex mirrors, or diverging mirrors, form virtual, diminished, and erect images regardless of the position of the object.
 
• They are commonly used in vehicles as rear-view mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Plane mirrors form virtual, erect images that are the same size as the object.
 
• The image formed is laterally inverted.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Mirrors**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in telescopes, headlights, and solar furnaces due to their converging properties.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in security and safety applications due to their wide field of view.

questions.question: Select the correct option for liquid connective tissue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Blood is considered a connective tissue because it has a matrix, called plasma, in which cells are suspended.
 
• It plays a crucial role in transporting nutrients, oxygen, and waste products throughout the body.
 
• Blood consists of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, each serving distinct functions.
 
• It helps in maintaining homeostasis by regulating pH, temperature, and water content of cells.
 
• Blood also plays a vital role in the immune system, helping to protect the body against diseases and infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cartilage**

 
 
• It is a flexible connective tissue found in joints, rib cage, ear, nose, bronchial tubes, and intervertebral discs.
 
• Cartilage provides support and cushioning to the body structures and is more rigid than muscle but more flexible than bone.
 
 
 
• **Adipose connective tissue**
 
 
• This tissue stores fat and provides insulation and cushioning for the body.
 
• It plays a role in energy storage and helps to protect organs.
 
 
 
• **Areolar connective tissue**
 
 
• This is a loose connective tissue that holds organs in place and attaches epithelial tissue to underlying tissues.
 
• It contains a variety of cell types and fibers that provide support and elasticity.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does NOT show asexual reproduction by means of fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthworm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leishmania reproduces asexually by binary fission, where the organism divides into two equal parts.
 
• Amoeba also undergoes binary fission, a type of asexual reproduction where the cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually and do not undergo asexual reproduction by means of fission.
 
• Plasmodium, the parasite responsible for malaria, reproduces asexually by multiple fission within the host's red blood cells and liver cells.
 
• Earthworms are hermaphrodites, meaning each individual possesses both male and female reproductive organs, and they reproduce through copulation and exchange of sperm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• A common method of asexual reproduction in prokaryotes and some single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Involves the division of a single organism into two parts, each of which grows into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where the nucleus divides multiple times before the cell splits into many new cells.
 
• Commonly seen in some protozoa and algae, like Plasmodium.
 
 
 
• **Hermaphroditism**
 
 
• A condition in which an organism has both male and female reproductive organs.
 
• Common in some invertebrates like earthworms, as well as in many plants.

questions.question: Which element is needed by the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

**__Note__:** As per the official answer key, the given answer is **Potassium** but in actual the correct answer would be __**Iodine**__ because the thyroid gland requires iodine to produce the hormone thyroxine (T4)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The thyroid gland requires iodine to produce the hormone thyroxine (T4).
 
• Thyroxine plays a crucial role in regulating metabolism, growth, and development.
 
• Iodine deficiency can lead to thyroid-related issues such as goiter and hypothyroidism.
 
• Seafood, dairy products, and iodized salt are good sources of dietary iodine.
 
• The recommended daily intake of iodine varies by age, gender, and physiological status (e.g., pregnancy).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium**

 
 
• Essential for maintaining fluid balance and nerve function.
 
• Commonly found in table salt and processed foods.
 
 
 
• **Calcium**
 
 
• Vital for bone health and muscle function.
 
• Found in dairy products, leafy greens, and fortified foods.
 
 
 
• **Potassium**
 
 
• Important for heart function and muscle contraction.
 
• Present in bananas, oranges, and potatoes.

questions.question: When white light is incident on a glass prism, it undergoes dispersion. This phenomenon is due to ________.

options.text: refractive index of the glass being different for different colours
refractive index of the glass being the same for different colours

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**refractive index of the glass being different for different colours**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The phenomenon of dispersion occurs when white light is split into its constituent colours.
 
• This happens because the refractive index of the glass prism is different for different wavelengths (colours) of light.
 
• Shorter wavelengths (blue/violet light) are refracted more than longer wavelengths (red light).
 
• As a result, each colour in the white light spectrum is bent by a different amount, creating a spectrum.
 
• Dispersion is a key principle in the formation of rainbows and the use of prisms in spectroscopy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interference of Light**

 
 
• Interference is the phenomenon where two waves superpose to form a resultant wave of greater or lesser amplitude.
 
• It is commonly observed in thin films and other wave-related experiments.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction of Light**
 
 
• Diffraction occurs when light waves bend around obstacles or pass through narrow openings, causing the waves to spread out.
 
• This phenomenon is significant in understanding wave behavior and is observed in various optical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with a different refractive index.
 
• This principle is essential in the design of lenses and other optical devices.

questions.question: A solution contains 40 g of common salt in 320 g of water. What is the concentration of the solution in terms of mass by mass percentage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• To determine the concentration of a solution in terms of mass by mass percentage, you need to divide the mass of the solute (common salt) by the total mass of the solution.
 
• The total mass of the solution is the sum of the mass of the solute and the solvent (water).
 
• In this case, the mass of the solute (common salt) is 40 g and the mass of the solvent (water) is 320 g.
 
• The total mass of the solution = 40 g + 320 g = 360 g.
 
• Mass by mass percentage = (Mass of solute / Total mass of solution) x 100 = (40 g / 360 g) x 100 = 11.11%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass by volume percentage**

 
 
• This is another common way to express the concentration of a solution, where the mass of the solute is divided by the volume of the solution, and the result is multiplied by 100.
 
 
 
• **Molarity**
 
 
• Molarity is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is a commonly used unit for expressing the concentration of a solution in chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Molality**
 
 
• Molality is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. This unit is useful in various chemical calculations, particularly when dealing with temperature changes.

questions.question: Which of the following substances can move across the cell membrane by diffusion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diffusion is a passive transport mechanism where substances move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• Oxygen is a small, nonpolar molecule that can easily diffuse across the cell membrane without the need for transport proteins.
 
• Nucleic acids, proteins, and starch are large molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by simple diffusion.
 
• The cell membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain molecules to pass through while blocking others.
 
• Oxygen diffusion is crucial for cellular respiration, a process that generates ATP, the energy currency of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Facilitated Diffusion**

 
 
• This process involves the use of transport proteins to move substances across the cell membrane.
 
• It is used for molecules that cannot diffuse directly through the lipid bilayer, such as glucose and amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport requires energy in the form of ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient.
 
• This process involves transport proteins such as pumps and is essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Endocytosis and Exocytosis**
 
 
• These are processes used by cells to transport large molecules or particles across the cell membrane.
 
• Endocytosis involves the engulfing of substances into the cell, while exocytosis involves the expulsion of substances from the cell.
